campaign: GNSS spoof step/ramp magnitude matrix (flight phase, no hard gate)
evidence_level: L2 (real firmware + 6DOF plant + sensor models, SIL only)

binary.note: source after reverting the snapshot jump guard; no aid/descent macros

scenario: 30 m hover, pos-hold at 20 s, 10 m N leg, spoof at 25 s, 45 s; 6 dirs x 10 seeds; no flow
modes: 0.1/0.5/1.0 m/s position ramp with consistent velocity

step20.note: NIS blocks the 20 m step; no drag

step30.note: 20 rejects/run then one reanchor; accepts the persistent offset, ~25 m error

verdict: The EKF is bounded but not spoof-resistant: 20 m steps are rejected by NIS; >=30 m steps are rejected for ~20 frames then re-anchored to the spoofed position, leaving ~0.83x step error; slow ramps are followed (0.1 m/s ~1 m, 0.5 m/s ~5 m, 1.0 m/s ~10 m by 45 s). Hard snapshot rejection starves GNSS and crashes; without an external reference a persistent offset is unobservable. Use bounded response/degradation or external aids, not hard rejection.
caveats: No flow in this matrix; a fresh horizontal external velocity source could detect the ramp if it disagrees with GNSS over time.
The reanchor is the existing persistent-implausible-GNSS logic; it keeps the vehicle airborne but accepts the spoofed coordinate.
All numbers are scalar-Eigen SIL L2, not real aircraft.
